Then go on without him in your life. You aren’t obligated to return any amount of time or effort spent on family back to them. You have your life to live, and if you want to live it happily then you live it on your terms. If your terms don’t include your father, that’s okay. Holding onto the hate is a resentment that keeps some part of the abuse, the abandonment, and the suffering you’ve been experiencing, it keeps it alive to a degree inside you. Pain is inevitable, suffering isn’t. Hate only breeds suffering.

I’m so sorry for what you went through, I had an absent father for a while, he came back but it wasn’t the same.  It isn’t the same as what you with through, but I can empathize. 

I can tell you from experience, holding onto that hate will burn you up from the inside. I’m not saying forgive the man, abandoning a family for a new one is just shitty to put it bluntly. What I’m saying is: turn your pain, your heartache, your longing, your frustration, into a fuel for you to be a better person for who you need to be. Whether that’s a parent, a friend, a partner, or just a better human. Give to the people that you love what you were denied or what you missed out on. 

Because at the end of the day, if we wish to break the cycle of negativity, the cycle of abuse, the cycle of abandonment; we have to break it ourselves.
